decisions.reason: The second V clause reports loss of an already-required right-arm reach and is already represented as a same-message runtime failure; the E/L design change does not modify the second V's requirement state.
The client says the Hero V has fulfilled its role and shifts attention to other letters, but does not change, defer, or remove its approved geometry requirements.
The peak-alignment refinement does not replace or alter the existing requirement that the accent be literally derived from the Hero V terminal.
The message's peak-alignment requirement is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE Event; the separate E/L modification adds nothing to it.
Changing the E and L letterform language does not necessarily change the established kerning or cohesive-reading requirement.
The E/L construction refinement contains no decision about champagne material treatment, color, or the finish requirement's deferred lifecycle.
The requested architectural E and L refinements remain compatible with the existing all-caps direction and do not change case treatment.
